newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-SCOTLAND LEFT RED-FACED IN ESTONIA "REPLAY".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCOTLAND LEFT RED-FACED IN ESTONIA "REPLAY".

text.p: Scotland were left red-faced when Estonia turned up on Tuesday and took a point from them in their World Cup qualifier after missing the original kick-off four months ago.
The Scots attacked for much of the game but scorned a number of chances in front of a crowd of about 4,000, about half of them Scottish fans.
When they were on target they found Estonian goalkeeper Mart Poom in inspired form and the European group four match ended goalless.
Scotland manager Craig Brown was so embarrassed by his side's display that he expressed "extreme disappointment and apologies" to the travelling fans.
They head the group table with eight points from four games but Brown said the Scots' inability to beat the Estonians would seriously damage their chances of qualifying for the finals.
Celtic defender Tom Boyd came closest to breaking the deadlock when he hit the bar in the first half, while Estonia's best chance fell to Andres Oper near the end.
The match was played in Monaco after a dispute over the floodlighting for the original match in Tallinn last October meant the Estonian team failed to turn up at a revised kick-off time.
Scotland were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory but Estonia appealed, securing the replay.
Estonia coach Teitur Thordarsson said in view of the result the appeal had been worthwhile.
He said he had expected the Scots to have created more chances.
While bemoaning his own team's performance, Brown said Estonia had shown they would be no pushovers for Austria and Sweden, Scotland's other main challengers in group four.
